source_text: Orationes contra Arianos (fragmenta) ΟΙ ΛΟΓΟΙ ΚΑΤΑ ΑΡΕΙΑΝΩΝ 54 Ἀλλ' οἱ παράδοξοι τῆς Ἀρείου θυμέλης μεσόχοροι τὸ μὲν ἁμαρτίαν πεποιηκέναι τὸν Χριστὸν φράζουσι· 55 Τὸ δὲ ὅτι Θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ, οὔτε ἐν μνήμῃ φέρουσιν οὔτε τοῖς τῆς γλώττης ὀργάνοις ἐκφωνοῦσιν. Ἀλλὰ ὥσπερ δεινοὶ συκοφάνται καὶ κατήγοροι ἀκρωτηριάσαντες τὸ χωρίον, τὸν ἀγῶνα τῆς κατηγορίας ποιοῦνται. 56 ∆εῖ δὲ φιλαλήθως τοὺς ἐννόμους ἀγωνιστὰς πάντα συμπεριλαβόντας ἀπαραλείπτως, ἀλλὰ μὴ πρὸς ἀπάτην μέρος μὲν ἀποσιωπᾶν, μέρος δὲ ἀποσπῶντας προφέρειν. 57 Εἰ γὰρ κτιστὸς οὐκ ἄρα γεννητός· εἰ δὲ γεννητὸς, οὐ κτιστός· ἐπεὶ μηδὲ οἷόν τε περὶ τὴν αὐτὴν φύσιν ἑκάτερον στρέφεσθαι τὸ γένος. 58 Πᾶν τὸ ἀρχὴν ἔχον καὶ τέλος ἐπιδέχεται, πᾶν τὸ τέλος ἐπιδεχόμενον φθορᾶς ἐστιν δεκτικόν.
thought_title: The Arians' selective quotation and the created/begotten antithesis
orientation: Eustathius opens his treatise by attacking how the Arians quote Scripture about Christ, then moves to the logical incompatibility of 'created' and 'begotten.'
pass_a_gloss: But the Arians, followers of Arius, say that Christ committed sin. But that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, they neither hold in memory nor utter aloud. But just as crafty false accusers and prosecutors, having mutilated the passage, they make the contest of accusation. But it is necessary truth-lovingly that lawful contenders, having embraced all things without omission, not for deception to silence one part, and tearing away another part to bring it forward. For if Christ is created, then not begotten; but if begotten, not created; since both categories cannot apply to the same nature. Everything that has a beginning also admits an end; everything that admits an end is capable of corruption.

lemmas.gloss: to silence, pass over in silence

choices.why: The term is theatrical, matching θυμέλης ('stage'); it suggests performers in the middle of the chorus, not a standard theological term.
The theatrical image of Arius's followers as performers on a stage carries Eustathius's mockery; 'stage' preserves the metaphor.
The glossary requires 'mutilating' for this term; the aorist participle keeps the completed action before the accusation.
The glossary requires 'false accusers'; it pairs with κατήγοροι ('prosecutors') to build the legal metaphor.
The glossary requires 'capable of corruption'; the construction with δεκτικόν plus genitive is rendered literally.
The glossary requires 'having a beginning'; the participial phrase is kept literal to preserve the logical chain.

pass_b_english: But the Arians, followers of Arius, say—as they claim—that Christ committed sin. Yet the words that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Corinthians 5:19) they neither hold in memory nor utter aloud. Instead, like crafty false accusers and prosecutors, they mutilate the passage and then make their case for the accusation. But lawful contenders must love the truth and embrace all things without omission, not silence one part and tear away another part to present it for deception. For if Christ is created, then he is not begotten; and if he is begotten, he is not created, since both categories cannot apply to the same nature. Everything that has a beginning also admits an end, and everything that admits an end is capable of corruption.
